code.note: The archive is a 2006 Fortran conversion by John Burkardt. Driver driver.f holds TOMS352_PRB. The shipped res is the reference output; its TEST05 section prints R, Q, Exact Value and Computed. Exact values come from mathieu_even_values in driver.f, which cites Abramowitz and Stegun Table 20.1. Subroutine MFCVAL is in src.f.

claim.location: Shipped reference output res, section TEST05 (even solutions), row R = 5, Q = 5, Computed column. The same row's Exact Value column is 25.549972. Claim value: a(5, 5) = 25.549972, computed by MFCVAL(N = 6, R = 5, Q = 5).

reference.sha256: not computed; the value is quoted here and compared as a number

claim.metric: Mathieu even characteristic value a_R(Q) at R = 5, Q = 5, as printed by the driver (g16.8).
claim.paper_value: The paper's own table is not read. The value is the shipped Exact column, which the archive attributes to Abramowitz and Stegun Table 20.1.

tolerance.basis: The reference prints 8 significant digits (rounding 5e-7 at this magnitude). 1e-5 absolute is about 4e-7 relative: it covers printed rounding and double-precision rounding in the eigenvalue iteration, and still catches a wrong eigenvalue, since the neighbouring rows differ by more than 1e-2. Fixed now, before any run; not to be loosened after a run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: the driver evaluates a few dozen cases.
cost.data_size: None: the test values are hard-coded in driver.f.
cost.data_licence: No data. Source is the public netlib TOMS collected-algorithms archive.

why: The driver computes the Mathieu characteristic value a_5(5) with MFCVAL and prints it next to the tabulated exact value, so a rerun must run the Fortran eigenvalue routine to reproduce the value; it is not a closed form.
